newsitem.title: USA: US Midwest direct hogs seen steady-up $1.00 -trade.
newsitem.headline: US Midwest direct hogs seen steady-up $1.00 -trade.

text.p: Midwest direct cash hog prices were seen steady to up $0.50 per cwt, instances $1.00 higher, on Monday as supplies continued to tighten going into the weekend, livestock dealers said.

Prices turned mostly $0.50-$1.00 per cwt higher on Friday as several meat packers were caught short on live inventory and had to aggressively bid for hogs to fill slaughter needs, sources said. Recent ideal corn harvesting weather has occupied farmers' time and led to light hog runs, they said.
Iowa and southern Minnesota top prices for hogs delivered to the plant could range from $54.00 to $54.50.
Illinois top prices at the plant could range from $53.00 to $53.50 and Indiana/Ohio top values were seen at $52.50 to $53.50, sources in those areas said.

But gains in cash hog prices Monday could be offset by ideas continued unprofitable operating margins would spur cutbacks in slaughter, market sources said. Sluggish pork demand reportedly put margins in a slump, they said.

Slaughter Friday was estimated at 358,000 head and Saturday at 43,000, which brought the week-to-date figure to 1.851 million head, USDA said. The weekly figure was less than one percent above last week and 7.5 percent below last year.
